llm.summary: This paid skill discloses a payment flow, but the artifacts are not coherent enough because they request credential and file access while the advertised document-preparation service is not actually implemented in the inspected runtime files.

dimensions.detail: Outbound network access to a fixed payment endpoint and local order-file reads/writes are broadly consistent with a paid service, but they are high-impact capabilities relative to the missing service implementation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer was found; the skill declares a dependency on clawtip-skill and explicitly directs use of the clawtip payment skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs a two-argument service command, but the service script accepts only one argument, and create_order.py has an indentation error that prevents order creation from running.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill reads payCredential from a persistent local order file and sends it to the remote payment service; this is partly disclosed, but there is no clear cleanup, retention boundary, or user confirmation gate before credential verification.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is software copyright application material assistance, but the executable flow only creates an order and verifies payment; it does not perform or return the advertised document-preparation work.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. It contacts a third-party payment service, stores order metadata locally, and uses a saved payCredential for verification, but the inspected scripts appear to provide payment verification rather than the promised document-preparation service. Install only if you trust the publisher and are comfortable with the local order-file and payment-credential flow.
llm.findings: [TP4] expected: Payment processing, remote verification, and local order metadata are disclosed and expected for a paid workflow, so the finding is not evidence of maliciousness by itself; the concern remains because credential handling and persistence are under-scoped and the actual service logic is absent/inconsistent.
